title: MER-Live: An Interactive Browser Demo of Prosody-Driven Multimodal Emotion Recognition
abstract: MER-Live is a real-time multimodal emotion recognition demo in which speech is the dominant signal, supported by video and lexical cues. The acoustic branch uses a novel lightweight masked auto-encoder SER model (MSMC) on log-mel spectrograms, while the text branch acts only as an auxiliary tie-breaker rather than a keyword trigger. Users speak to the camera and watch emotion estimates update four times per second. They can hot-swap ten speaker-holdout checkpoints, record a five second utterance for IEMOCAP-style logit averaging, or upload audio files for side-by-side comparison with an open SER baseline. The 6.77M-parameter audio model, exported to TensorRT FP16, serves a batch of five in 0.24 ms on one H200, giving a 14x speed-up over PyTorch FP32. On 10-fold IEMOCAP, the deployed audio-only MSMC checkpoint used in MER-Live reaches 74.03% WA and 66.39% UA. Multimodal performance exceeds 83%.
relevance_note: Real-time multimodal emotion recognition demo; no synthesis.
